content: Administer approximately 6 grams of the medication intravaginally, either once daily or every 12 hours, for a duration of 30 days. The safety and efficacy of this treatment have not been fully established. Local sensitivity reactions, such as discomfort or burning sensations, may occur. Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides is a contraindication. Use during the third trimester of pregnancy is not recommended due to potential risks. Severe hematologic reactions, including aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis, and other blood dyscrasias, have been reported. Additionally, severe dermatologic reactions, such as toxic epidermal necrolysis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome, have been documented. Cases of fulminant hepatic necrosis have also been reported with the use of sulfonamides, regardless of the route of administration. If a skin rash or other hypersensitivity reaction occurs, discontinue the medication immediately. This medication is classified as Pregnancy Category C, indicating that risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. Its use during lactation is not recommended. The drug exerts a bacteriostatic effect by inhibiting para-aminobenzoic acid, thereby interfering with microbial folic acid synthesis and growth.
